message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on highways with 2–3 lanes per direction.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted). | | **Seat‑belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years or under 4 ft 9 in must be in a child safety seat. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held devices are prohibited while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers and drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has priority.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Passing on the right is prohibited unless the left lane is occupied. | | **Parking** | • No parking within 15 ft of a stop sign, crosswalk, or intersection.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to pick up/drop off children. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing is allowed only if the vehicle is not moving.
• Tow‑away laws require a tow‑away permit for removal of abandoned vehicles. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Registration must be renewed annually.
• Vehicles must pass an annual safety inspection (except exempt categories). | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red light: stop; Yellow: prepare to stop; Green: proceed.
• Stop signs: come to a complete stop before proceeding. | | **Special Rules** | • “No‑stop” zones: no stopping or parking.
• “No‑passing” zones: no passing on the right. | ### How to Find Detailed Statutes - **Texas Transportation Code** – Sections 545.001–545.999 cover most traffic laws. - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Provides driver’s handbook and updates. - **Texas Legislature Online** – Search for bills or statutes by keyword. ### Common Enforcement Practices - Police may issue tickets for speeding, seat‑belt violations, cell‑phone use, and DUI. - Repeat offenders face higher fines, points on their driving record, and possible license suspension. --- If you need specific legal advice or want to look into recent court cases involving Texas traffic law, let me know!
